sentences.text: This appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 has been preferred by the appellants/Claimants against the award dated 09.01.2019 passed by the learned First Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Raigarh (for short,'Claims Tribunal'), in Claim Case-56 of 2018 for enhancement of the compensation awarded by the Tribunal.

entities.text: First Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Raigarh
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
By the impugned award, learned Claims Tribunal awarded compensation of Rs.6,77,500/- to the appellants/claimants on account of death of deceased- Yashoda Rathiya, wife of appellant-1, and Dhaneshwar vs Pawan Kumar Upadhyay on 13 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/18322427/
1 mother of appellants-2 and 3, who died in a motor accident on 01.11.2017 by rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle, Passenger Bus bearing registration No.CG-13 D-3923, driven by respondent-1 PawanKumar Upadhyay, owned by respondent-2 Akhtar Ali Rijvi Momin, and insured by the Insurance Company, respondent-3.

3. As per the pleadings, the deceased-Yashoda Rathiya was working as Tailor, and was earning Rs.300-400/- per day and thus, Rs.10,000/- per month, and the appellants are dependents on the income of the deceased.
4. Respondents-1 and 2, driver and owner of the offending vehicle have pleaded that no accident took place on 01.11.2017, and there is no evidence regarding her income, hence, excessive amount has been claimed by the claimants.
5. Respondent-3, Insurance Company filed its written statement and denied the averment of claim petition and pleaded that the driver of offending vehicle was not having a valid and effective driving license at the time of accident and there is breach of Policy condition. Deceased was not died on account of motor accident.
The offending vehicle was being driven in violation of Policy conditions as there is no permit for the same, and therefore, Insurance Company is not liable to pay compensation to the claimants.

On the basis of above pleadings, learned Tribunal has framed five issues and after appreciating the material available on record, decided the same in favour of the appellants/claimants, and considered the monthly income of the deceased as Rs.4,500/- on Notional basis and awarded the compensation as stated above.
7.

Shri Manoj Jaiswal, learned counsel for the appellants would submit that deceased Yashoda Rathiya was aged about 40 years at the time of accident, skilled labour and was working as Tailor,
hence, her income ought to have been considered as Rs.10,000/ per month.

In alternate, he submits that looking to the date of accident, prevailing minimum wages on the date of accident should have been taken for assessing the compensation and amount awarded towards other conventional heads also on lower side, and therefore, the amount of compensation is liable to be enhanced suitably.

8. Shri Robin Aryalal, learned counsel appearing on behalf of Shri Ghanshyam Patel, learned counsel for respondent-3 supports the award passed by the learned Claims Tribunal and would submit that the Tribunal has rightly considered the monthly income of the deceased on Notional basis and there is no document with respect to the income of the deceased.
Therefore, amount awarded by the Claims Tribunal is just and proper, which needs no interference by this Court.

9. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the perused the evidence available on record.
Mac 137 of 2020 Dhaneshwar vs Pawan Kumar Upadhyay on 13 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/18322427/
2 10.
Barring the oral evidence of the appellants/claimants, no document with respect to the profession/income of the deceased has been filed.

However, looking to the date of accident, nature of job and minimum wages prescribed on the prevailing date of the accident, this Court is of the considered view that Rs.7,500/- can be safely taken as monthly income of the deceased at the time of accident.

11. In light of above, and taking guidance from the decisions of Hon'ble Supreme Court in cases of National Insurance Company Limited v. Pranay Sethi and Others (2017) 16 SCC 680, Magma General Insurance Company Limited v. Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram and Others (2018) 18 SCC 130 and in case of Smt Sarla Verma and others Vs Delhi Transport Corporation and others (2009) 6 SCC 121, this court is recomputing the compensation as below:

sentences.text: Notional income of the claimant is being taken as Rs.7,500/- per month, and Rs.90,000/- per annum (7500x12)

By adding 40% of the income towards future prospects as has been considered in case of Pranay Sethi (supra), annual income of the deceased comes to Rs.1,26,000/- {90000 + (90000x40/100)}.
Out of annual income of the deceased 1/3 rd personal expenditure to be deducted,
now yearly income of the deceased comes to Rs.84,000/- {126000  (126000 x 1/3)}.
Deceased was aged about 40 years at the time of accident and the accident is of the year 2017, therefore, in view of Smt Sarla Verma Vs Delhi Transport Corporation (2009) 6 SCC 121, multiplier of 15 would be applicable to calculate the total loss of dependency, which comes to Rs.12,60,000/- (84000 x 15).
Rs.40,000/- Consortium to each of the appellants/claimants, Funeral expenses- 15,000/-, Loss of estate-Rs.15,000/-.
Mac 137 of 2020 Now total compensation comes to Rs.14,10,000/- (1260000 + 120000 + 15000 +
15000)
12.

The amount of compensation of Rs.6,77,500/- already awarded by the Tribunal is now enhanced to Rs.14,10,000/-.
Thereby, the claimants are now entitled for additional amount of Rs.7,32,500/- (1410000  677500).
the additional amount shall carry interest @ 6% per annum from the date of claim application till its realization.
The impugned award stands modified to the extent indicated herein above.
13. The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the amount of compensation enhanced by this Court within a period of 60 days from today.

On such deposit by the Insurance Company,
Rs.5,00,000/- shall be deposited in name of appellants- 2 and 3 for a period of three years in Fixed Deposit at any Nationalized bank.
Remaining amount shall be paid to the appellants/claimants through Bank transaction/account payee cheque.
